title: Defense first: TAMIU Dustdevils enter 2026-27 with 15 newcomers and a new identity
excerpt: TAMIU men's basketball enters the 2026-27 season with 15 newcomers, a defense-first identity under seventh-year head coach Mac McConnell, and a season opener at Oklahoma Baptist on Nov. 13, according to TAMIU Athletics.
content:
Texas A&M International University men's basketball enters the 2026-27 season with a revamped roster and renewed expectations under head coach Mac McConnell, who returns for his seventh season, according to TAMIU Athletics.

The Dustdevils are coming off an 8-20 campaign, including a 5-15 record in Lone Star Conference play, and welcome 15 newcomers as they look to take a step forward in one of NCAA Division II's most competitive conferences, according to TAMIU Athletics.

Despite being picked 15th in the Lone Star Conference preseason poll, McConnell emphasized chemistry, toughness, and commitment to the program's culture, according to TAMIU Athletics. He said the team has scrimmaged three different teams in October and has improved each time out.

Among the returning players is guard Aaron Perez, named a preseason player to watch for the Dustdevils, according to TAMIU Athletics. Perez appeared in 20 games last season, making 12 starts and averaging 6.2 points per game, with a season-high 24 points against UT Permian Basin on Jan. 22. Guard Luke Oxford also returns, and senior forward Thomas Tangle joins as a transfer from Cameron University, where he averaged 9.5 points per game last season.

McConnell said the team's identity will begin on defense, paired with an up-tempo offense, and that if the group stays healthy and keeps building chemistry, he can see it making the Lone Star Conference tournament, according to TAMIU Athletics.

The Dustdevils open the season on the road against Oklahoma Baptist University on Friday, Nov. 13, at 7:30 p.m. in Shawnee, Oklahoma, according to TAMIU Athletics.

Sources:

  • TAMIU Athletics, "Defense, Depth and Determination Highlight Dustdevils' 2026-27 Outlook," November 4, 2026
